Rehoboth by the River
reh-HOH-both
proper noun
Hebrew Rechoboth ha-Nahar, “broad places by the river”; from rachab, to be wide; the city of Saul (Shaul), king of Edom.

Biblical Definition

Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in Edom: “And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead” (Gen 36:37). The name Rehoboth means broad places, room, wide streets — a city of spacious ways set beside a river. It sounds like blessing, like the enlargement Isaac once named when the LORD made room for him and he was fruitful in the land. But this Rehoboth belonged to Edom, and its breadth was for a season only. The LORD maketh room for whom He will; He set the bounds of the nations and gave to Esau the mount of Seir for a possession. Yet room granted to the reprobate line is not the everlasting inheritance. Edom had her broad places and her river-city, and where are they now? The streets are silence, the kingdom a list of dead kings. The saint learns here to weigh what breadth is worth the having. There is a room the world gives, wide and pleasant for a day; and there is the place the Lord prepares, “a better country, that is, an heavenly” (Heb 11:16). Better a narrow gate that opens on the city of God than all the broad ways of Edom. The LORD who setteth thy foot in a large place hath set thee there for glory, not for a passing reign beside a fading river.

Webster 1828 Definition

The broad-streeted river-city of Saul, king of Edom (Gen 36:37); a witness that the room the LORD grants the reprobate line is only for a season, while His people seek an abiding city.

expand to see more

REHOBOTH BY THE RIVER, the city of Saul, king of Edom.

The name means broad places, room, wide streets by a river (Gen 36:37).

It echoes the enlargement the LORD once gave to Isaac.

Yet Edom's breadth was granted only for a season.

The saint seeks the broad room of the heavenly city instead.

Key Scripture

Gen 36:37 — "And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead."

Gen 36:36 — "And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead."

Heb 11:16 — "But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city."

Heb 13:14 — "For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come."

Modern Corruption

The river-city of an Edomite king, named for its broad places; it recovers the truth that room granted to the reprobate line lasts but a season.

expand to see more

A broad-streeted Edomite town raises no live modern quarrel. Its lesson is that the LORD makes room for whom He will, gave Esau his portion in Seir, yet reserved the abiding inheritance for the elect.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the difference between the world's broad room and God's everlasting place. Rehoboth's wide streets fell silent; the kingdom became a roll of dead kings. Better the narrow gate that opens on the city that hath foundations than all the broad ways of a passing Edom.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Rechoboth, from rachab, to be wide; hence broad places, streets, or room, here joined to “the river.”

expand to see more

Rehoboth by the River — the city of Saul, king of Edom (Gen 36:37).

From rachab, to be wide or roomy.

Hence “broad places,” wide streets, or room.

Distinguished from the wells of Rehoboth that Isaac dug (Gen 26).

The seventh-named king in the Edomite roll of Genesis 36.

Usage

"Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned after Samlah."

"Rehoboth means broad places, a city of wide streets."

"Edom's Rehoboth had room only for a season."
